newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria farm experts urge price liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria farm experts urge price liberalisation.

text.p: Bulgaria should liberalise prices of agricultural produce and restructure production units to boost domestic output, experts from the Bulgarian Agricultural Academy said on Tuesday.

"It is not realistic to expect that government subsidies should provide long term support for domestic agricultural production if local purchase prices are lower than international ones," Ranguel Trendafilov, head of the Agricultural Economics Institute, told a news conference.
Trendafilov said the government should seek restructuring of existing co-operative farms into efficient production units and leave pricing problems to be resolved by supply and demand.
BAA research units have raised wheat seed production to 5,000 tonnes for 1997 from 2,800 tonnes in 1996.

"The BAA can meet the country's demands for wheat seed but we are not optimistic about this year's harvest because only 25-28 percent of sown areas have been treated with pesticides and fertilisers and the yield is expected around three tonnes per hectare, down from 4.2 tonnes per hectare in 1989," said Petar Ivanov, head of the Wheat and Barley Research Institute.
Agriculture Minister Roumen Hristov said last week that Bulgaria needed to import 450,000 tonnes of wheat to meet demand until the new crop.
